LABEL: no vulnerability found
FUNCTION: The input is directly interpolated into a SQL query string — never parameterized.
RISK: No escaping is applied; an attacker can inject arbitrary SQL that the database executes against any role with read or execute on tables.

LABEL: hardcoded secret — sensitive data is embedded in source code
FUNCTION: A live production key is hard-coded into the module.
RISK: Anyone with access to the binary can reproduce the leak; no mitigation is possible without redeploying.

LABEL: no vulnerability found
FUNCTION: The same command is executed in a subprocess with no sensitive data.
RISK: None — there are no security vulnerabilities to detect.

LABEL: eval — arbitrary code execution from untrusted input
FUNCTION: A user-supplied string was passed to Python's built-in eval().
RISK: The attacker executes arbitrary Python code; a session can now steal cookies, take over the account, or restart the server.

LABEL: no vulnerability found
FUNCTION: A common salted hash function with a fixed salt length.
RISK: none — secure.

LABEL: no vulnerability found
FUNCTION: The request is made over HTTPS; the CA bundle is verified.
RISK: none — the issue is not present.

LABEL: no vulnerability found
FUNCTION: The request path is a static directory, not a file upload.
RISK: None — the issue does not exist.

LABEL: xss, cross-site scripting, innerHTML
FUNCTION: Untrusted content is inserted into the DOM without escaping.
RISK: The attacker injects script that runs in the victim's browser, stealing cookies or performing actions as the user.

LABEL: no vulnerability found
FUNCTION: The request path is not sensitive; it does not contain user input.
RISK: None — the endpoint has no security impact.

LABEL: no vulnerability found
FUNCTION: The same function is unchanged from a previous audit.
RISK: none — the code does not leak any sensitive information.

LABEL: strict-transport-security, content-security-policy, x-frame-options, x-content-type-options, x-xss-protection
FUNCTION: Production responses omit default CORS/HTTP headers that expose defaults policies.
RISK: Without these, the response allows XSS/FPS without a Content Security Policy.

LABEL: httponly, samesite, secure
FUNCTION: The session cookie is set without HttpOnly, SameSite=None, and Secure.
RISK: JavaScript can read it, cross-site attacks can send it without HTTPS.

LABEL: https, redirect, hsts
FUNCTION: The site is reachable over clear HTTP in addition to HTTPS.
RISK: Users on clear connect are subject to man-in-the-middle and session ID theft; cookies are no longer secure.

LABEL: content-security-policy, script, xss
FUNCTION: No Content-Security-Policy is set, or it allows unsafe-inline scripts.
RISK: Injected script has no source restriction, so XSS is unconstrained.

LABEL: directory listing, file exposure, enumeration
FUNCTION: The web server lists directory contents when no index file is present.
RISK: Sensitive files (backups, configs, source) are enumerated and downloaded by any visitor.

LABEL: stack trace, information disclosure, verbose error, leak
FUNCTION: Unhandled exceptions return full stack traces and framework internals to the client.
RISK: Attackers learn file paths, library versions, and query structure, accelerating exploitation.

LABEL: https, tls, plaintext, sniff, credentials
FUNCTION: Data is transmitted over the unencrypted internet — the network is a wire that carries plaintext.
RISK: Credentials and session cookies reach users over the network; anyone on the path reads them; attackers can sniff or modify them, too.

LABEL: hash, plaintext, storage, access, encrypt, database
FUNCTION: Passwords are stored in plaintext in the database.
RISK: Users who have access to the database also get a copy of the encrypted passwords; future logins validate the hash against the database instead of the password entry field.

LABEL: outdated, pin, semver, lockfile, dependency
FUNCTION: The package manager knows nothing about the dependency's semver range.
RISK: Any published version outside that range can break end-users' deployments, including critical ones.

LABEL: common vulnerability disclosure, cve, identifier, registry
FUNCTION: A CVE is a unique, public string identifier for a known vulnerability.
RISK: Without a CVE there is no standard means to sort and rank matches, so false positives abound.

LABEL: bandit, black, flake8, mypy, pyupgrade, safety, pylint
FUNCTION: A codebase with no known security or quality issues.
RISK: There is no scanner to run; there are no known vulnerabilities.

LABEL: npx audit, npm audit, npm, yarn, yarn
FUNCTION: npm/yarn run an internal dependency-scan against installed packages.
RISK: A vulnerable package is not exposed if npm/yarn are not invoked — a full scan must be scheduled.

LABEL: package-lock.json, pin, lock, version
FUNCTION: The lock file links specific versions to avoid installer ambiguity in future installs.
RISK: A dev dependency update can break all installs due to library instability; the lock re-links to a consistent set.

LABEL: typosquat, typo, subdomain, domain, registration
FUNCTION: Users must resolve typosquatting subdomains (sub.tld) to servers not authorized by the primary domain.
RISK: As users migrate to subdomains, they are less protected by host header matching and can now land on any server registered under the domain.

LABEL: abandoned, unmaintained, orphaned, dead, maintenance, support
FUNCTION: A maintained dependency has been orphaned: no maintainer is still actively developing it.
RISK: The project may go to EOL or enter a new unsupported state; new vulnerabilities are unpatched for at least 6 months.

LABEL: digest, tag, latest, vulnerable, pull
FUNCTION: Multiple tags identify an image; 'latest' is not always what you mean.
RISK: Pulling with a tag pins the image to a known digest, but "latest" can still be vulnerable.

LABEL: k6, vus, iterations, duration
FUNCTION: A k6 script defines a fixed-vus loop with number of iterations and duration.
RISK: Without a loop the test would fire once and exit, missing load.

LABEL: percentiles — 95, 98, 99
FUNCTION: The outer tail: 95th, 98th, 99th percentiles (longest observed latencies).
RISK: Without them, you have no sense of the worst-case latency; the service might be fine most of the time but just occasionally fall into a long stall.

LABEL: requests/second, rps, concurrent user, throughput
FUNCTION: RPS is throughput (requests completed per time); concurrency is how many in-flight requests the system serves at once.
RISK: Modeling only throughput (RPM) without concurrency underloades idle sessions but saturates busy ones; dashboards show both.

LABEL: logs, metrics, monitoring, cpu, memory, slow query, database
FUNCTION: Compare before/after graphs against standard workloads to locate the cause.
RISK: Without a metric trail you cannot isolate the effect of each change and scale back.

LABEL: leak, heap, profile, memory, gc
FUNCTION: A retained-reference reference-allocated object never gets collected.
RISK: Until the heap is exhausted the process stays responsive but consumes memory; eventually the system runs out of address space.

LABEL: connection pool, database, exhaust, fallback, leak, mutex, poison, queue, reload, sample, slow, tcp, timeout
FUNCTION: The fault is a thread or connection leak, a metric histogram fails to sample, or a handler logic bypasses the health check.
RISK: The service falls over until an end-user request kills it, escalating to a full-scale DDoS.

LABEL: canary, gradual, rollout, percentage
FUNCTION: A canary routes a small percentage of traffic to the new build, watches error/latency metrics, and rolls forward only if they hold.
RISK: A full rollout of a bad build takes everything down at once; a canary bounds the blast radius.

LABEL: 502 proxy, upstream down, service unavailable
FUNCTION: The target host is unreachable during the request path; 502 Back-pressure is returned to the client.
RISK: The target is down; users see either the soft or hard timeout error page and the session is lost.
